# RFC-0003: Teams, ownership, and policy-based authorization

> **Version:** 0.1.0 | **Status:** normative | **Phase:** spec
> **Owners:** @Will Eaton

---

## 1. Summary

### [RFC-0003:C-CONTEXT] Context and goals (Informative) <a id="rfc-0003c-context"></a>

The controller authorizes today through three unrelated mechanisms: a global two-tier role ladder configured by login lists, principal ownership on secrets and personal dispatch targets, and a source-forge approver allowlist. Ownership is recorded on standing launches but never consulted on edit or delete, a team cannot own a schedule, ownership alone never suffices without a global role, every read surface is open to any authenticated caller, and an agent inside a run acts with its launcher's full authority. This RFC defines one authorization contract: an open principal registry that adds controller-managed teams (composed of users, groups, rules, and other teams) and run principals; an owner on every governed resource with per-resource shares and a parent relation; a single deny-by-default decision bound to every route; and a policy set with a published schema that expresses roles, ownership rules, shares, expiry, dispatch admission, and approver sets as data. The decisions that define the secrets registry and brought clusters will be amended to defer to it on who may act. It does not prescribe a policy engine, a storage layout, an evaluation architecture, or a user interface framework; those choices belong in decision records that reference this RFC.

*Since: v0.1.0*

---

## 2. Specification

### [RFC-0003:C-PRINCIPALS] Principals (Normative) <a id="rfc-0003c-principals"></a>

A principal is `<scheme>:<id>`. Schemes are registered: this RFC registers `user`, `group`, `team`, and `run`, and a later amendment MAY register more. The policy schema of [RFC-0003:C-POLICY](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-policy) MUST be versioned over the registered schemes, and a principal whose scheme is not registered MUST deny. `user:<login>` and `team:<slug>` MUST be stored and compared lowercased and trimmed. `group:<path>` MUST be stored and compared exactly as the identity layer normalizes it, applied identically at write and at comparison, so that distinct identity-provider groups are never merged by the controller. A team slug MUST match `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{1,62}` and MUST be unique per controller. User and group principals MUST derive from a controller-validated identity (the session, token, or key the controller itself verified); a caller MUST NOT be able to assert a group by supplying it in a request. Team principals MUST derive from the controller's own team membership records; run principals from [RFC-0003:C-RUN-PRINCIPAL](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-run-principal). Every request has a subject, the principal set the decision evaluates, and an actor, the principal that caused the request: the authenticated user for an interactive or API-key call, the submitter when a portal records one, otherwise the owner principal of the launch or standing launch that fired. Subject and actor coincide for interactive and API-key calls and differ for firings, portal submissions, and runs. The subject set is the subject's own principal, every group principal the credential proves, and every team principal whose membership those principals satisfy under [RFC-0003:C-TEAMS](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-teams). The group refresh window is the configured interval at which the identity layer re-reads a credential's groups from the identity provider; a downgraded session is one whose refresh the provider refused. A credential that cannot prove groups (a static token, a cluster token, a downgraded session) MUST act as its user principal plus the team memberships whose derivation contains no group or rule member, including through nested teams, and MUST NOT act as any group-derived or rule-derived membership.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0003:C-TEAMS] Teams (Normative) <a id="rfc-0003c-teams"></a>

A team is a controller-managed record with a unique slug, a display name, and a member set. Each member MUST be a user principal, a group principal, another team, or a membership rule, paired with a team role. Team roles are totally ordered `member` < `maintainer` < `owner`; an amendment adding a role MUST place it in this order. A membership rule is a predicate over attributes of a controller-validated identity (at least: email domain, and group path prefix); it MUST be evaluated only against attributes the identity layer verified, and a change to a rule MUST be audited like a change to a listed member. Team membership MUST form a directed acyclic graph and a membership that would close a cycle MUST be refused. Along a nesting path the conferred role is the minimum of the roles on that path; a user's role in a team is the maximum over all paths that reach them. Group-derived and rule-derived membership MUST reflect the identity provider within one group refresh window. A team is itself a governed resource whose owner principal is the team; a team is not transferable and `transfer` on a team MUST deny. On creation the request MUST list at least one member at the `owner` role that currently resolves to a user; absent an explicit list, the creator is listed at `owner`. Creating a team, changing its members, rules, or roles, renaming it, and deleting it MUST be authorized by the decision in [RFC-0003:C-DECISION](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-decision) and audited as [RFC-0003:C-AUDIT](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-audit) requires. A team MUST NOT be deleted while it owns any other governed resource; the refusal MUST name the blocking resources the caller may read and the count of any others. A team none of whose memberships currently resolve to any user MUST remain the owner of its resources and MUST be listed as unreachable in the team listing available to platform administrators. Platform administration MUST be a team, so that administrator membership can be held through a group and changed without a redeploy.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0003:C-OWNERSHIP] Ownership of governed resources (Normative) <a id="rfc-0003c-ownership"></a>

Every governed resource MUST carry exactly one owner principal that is a user or a team. The governed resources are: registered playbooks, playbook drafts, pack imports, autoresearch scopes, standing launches and their triggers (schedules, watches, portals), one-shot launches, runs, secrets and their bindings, model providers and dispatch defaults scoped below the platform, dispatch targets including brought clusters, API keys, policy sets, teams, and every child resource named in [RFC-0003:C-HIERARCHY](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-hierarchy). An API key's owner MUST be the user it acts as. For a root resource the owner MUST be chosen by the creator from the principals the request acts as, defaulting to the creator's user principal; a creator MUST NOT set an owner they do not act as, and acting as the intended owner is necessary and not sufficient: `create` on that owner is still decided by policy. For a child resource the owner is its parent's owner and is not chosen; `create` on the child is decided against the parent's owner and scope. The owner MUST NOT change except through the `transfer` action on a root resource. Ownership MUST be transferable only to a principal the transferring caller acts as or, for a platform administrator, to any user or team; a transfer that would collide with an identifier the new owner already holds under [RFC-0003:C-NAMES](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-names) MUST be refused; and every transfer MUST be audited. A resource whose owner is a team MUST remain usable when any individual member leaves; a resource whose owner is a user MUST remain visible to platform administrators so it can be transferred when the user departs.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0003:C-ACTIONS] Action vocabulary (Normative) <a id="rfc-0003c-actions"></a>

Authorization MUST be expressed over a fixed, documented action vocabulary per resource type, using stable identifiers of the form `<resource>:<verb>`. Every resource type MUST define at least `read`, `create`, `update`, `delete`, `transfer`, and `share`; playbooks, drafts, and standing launches MUST additionally define `launch`; imports, scopes, and drafts (graduation) MUST define `approve`; secrets MUST define `bind` and `rotate`; dispatch targets MUST define `dispatch`; runs MUST define `publish`; drafts MUST define `publish`, registration into the registry without review, which a rule deriving from ownership alone MUST NOT grant; policy sets MUST define `activate`; teams MUST define `manage-members`. `transfer` on a child resource resolves to `transfer` on its root under [RFC-0003:C-HIERARCHY](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-hierarchy). The vocabulary MUST be retrievable from the API by any authenticated user principal. Adding an action is a compatible change; renaming or removing one is a breaking change under the RFC lifecycle. A request naming an action or resource type outside the vocabulary MUST be refused.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0003:C-DECISION] One authorization decision (Normative) <a id="rfc-0003c-decision"></a>

Every API operation MUST be authorized by one decision that takes: the subject principal set and the team role held under each team principal in it; the actor; one action from [RFC-0003:C-ACTIONS](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-actions); the resource type, the resource's owner principal, its ancestor chain under [RFC-0003:C-HIERARCHY](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-hierarchy), and where the action is `dispatch` the resolved target (or, for `create` and listing, the resource type with the intended owner and parent); the active policy set; the shares on the resource and its ancestors; and the current time. It MUST answer allow or deny with a structured reason naming the rule that decided or the absence of one. The decision MUST be deny by default: an empty subject set, an action outside the vocabulary, or an unresolvable resource MUST deny. The same decision MUST serve the browser, the API-key path, the MCP surface, run principals, and non-interactive re-checks, so that what a preview shows, what a launch is refused with, and what a firing standing launch may do agree. A standing launch, watch, or portal MUST fire with its owner as subject and that owner's memberships resolved at firing time, never from a stored snapshot; when the owner is a team, the firing's subject is that team principal at the `maintainer` role. The actor of a firing is the submitter when one exists, otherwise the owner. A firing whose owner cannot be resolved (a deleted user, a team with no resolvable member) or whose decision denies MUST be refused, handled under [RFC-0001:C-RECURRING-POLICY](../rfc/RFC-0001.md#rfc-0001c-recurring-policy), and audited. An `update` that changes what a standing launch fires (its playbook, inputs, resolved target, or bindings) MUST additionally be decided as a launch by the updating subject, who MUST hold `launch` on the playbook, `dispatch` on the resolved target, and `bind` on each bound secret, or the update MUST be refused. Roles, ownership, team membership, shares, and approver sets MUST all be inputs to this one decision; an endpoint MUST NOT consult an independent allowlist, environment list, or role check instead of it. Disclosure of a denial is governed by [RFC-0003:C-READ-SCOPING](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-read-scoping).

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0003:C-ENFORCEMENT] Enforcement at the boundary (Normative) <a id="rfc-0003c-enforcement"></a>

Every served route MUST be bound to exactly one action and one resource resolution, and a request to a route with no binding MUST be denied for every caller. The route-to-action bindings MUST be retrievable so that conformance can be checked against the served route table. A response MUST NOT reflect any effect of a request the decision denied. A list MAY be narrowed only by applying the same decision per item. Machine surfaces that authenticate by a pod-bound credential rather than a principal (the ingest drop-box, metrics) are outside this contract and MUST NOT be granted any action from [RFC-0003:C-ACTIONS](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-actions).

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0003:C-POLICY] Policy as stored, validated data (Normative) <a id="rfc-0003c-policy"></a>

The rules the decision evaluates MUST be a policy set with a published schema over the principal, action, and resource vocabularies of this RFC. A policy set MUST be validated against that schema before it becomes active, and an invalid set MUST be refused with the failing rule named. Validation MUST also refuse a set that grants `manage-members` or `transfer` on a team to a role below `owner`, and a set under which no user or team principal would hold `activate`. The active policy set MUST be identified by a content digest, and the policy set is a governed resource read through the `read` action, which the default policy set MUST grant to all authenticated user principals. The controller MUST ship a default policy set that grants: a user owner every action on the resources they own; on a team-owned resource, the team's `member` role `read` and `launch`, the `maintainer` role additionally `create`, `update`, `bind`, and `rotate`, and the `owner` role every action including `transfer`, `share`, `delete`, and `manage-members`; every authenticated user principal `dispatch` on a dispatch target owned by the platform administrator team, matching the open default of the cluster policy it replaces; and the platform administrator team every action on every resource. Activating a policy set is the `activate` action, decided by the policy in force at that moment, and MUST be audited with the prior and new digests.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0003:C-APPROVALS] Approvers as policy (Normative) <a id="rfc-0003c-approvals"></a>

Who may approve a pack import, a scope, or a draft graduation MUST be decided by the `approve` action through [RFC-0003:C-DECISION](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-decision), with approver sets expressed as team roles or policy rules rather than a separate allowlist. An approval recorded from an external system (a source-forge review) MUST be attributed to a controller identity through a verified account link: an association between the external login and a controller user that the user established while authenticated to both. An external login with no verified link MUST NOT approve. Any existing approver allowlist or forge-association fallback MUST be honoured only through an explicit policy rule that names it, so that removing the rule removes the path.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0003:C-READ-SCOPING] Read scoping (Normative) <a id="rfc-0003c-read-scoping"></a>

Reading a governed resource is the `read` action and MUST be authorized like any other. A list endpoint MUST return only the items the caller may read and MUST NOT reveal whether items were withheld. When a caller lacks `read` on a resource, every action on that resource MUST return the same response as for a resource that does not exist; the structured denial of [RFC-0003:C-DECISION](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-decision) is returned only when the caller may read the resource. A child resource is read under its parent's scope as [RFC-0003:C-HIERARCHY](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-hierarchy) defines, and a resource's shares are read with it. Team memberships and the active policy set are governed resources read under the same rule.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0003:C-CREDENTIAL-PARITY] Credential parity (Normative) <a id="rfc-0003c-credential-parity"></a>

The decision MUST produce the same answer for the same user regardless of which credential proves them, provided the credential proves the same groups. An API key MUST act with the owner's group memberships as refreshed within the group refresh window that governs sessions; a key whose owner's groups cannot be refreshed within that window MUST act as the user principal plus directly listed team memberships until they can. Revoking a team membership or a group MUST take effect for every credential of the affected user within one group refresh window. The identity probe MUST state whether the presenting credential proves groups.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0003:C-AUDIT] Audit (Normative) <a id="rfc-0003c-audit"></a>

The controller MUST record an audit event for: team creation, membership, rule, and role changes, and deletion; ownership assignment at creation and every transfer; share grant, change, and revocation; activation of a policy set; issuance of a run credential; and every denied mutation. Each record MUST carry the actor, the subject when it differs, the credential path that proved the request, the action, the resource type and identifier, the rule that decided, the prior and resulting state where the operation changed one, and the time. An operation whose audit record cannot be persisted MUST fail. Audit records MUST be retrievable by the owner of the affected resource, by the affected team's owners, and by platform administrators, under the read scoping of the resource they concern. This extends [RFC-0001:C-AUDIT](../rfc/RFC-0001.md#rfc-0001c-audit) from administrator policy changes to authorization changes generally.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0003:C-COMPATIBILITY] Compatibility and migration (Normative) <a id="rfc-0003c-compatibility"></a>

Adoption MUST NOT grant any principal an action the prior mechanisms denied, except grants the active policy set makes explicitly to user owners, team roles, and shares, and every such grant MUST be attributable to a policy rule. Existing governed resources MUST be backfilled with an owner in this precedence: the recorded owner snapshot if present, else the recorded creator, else the platform administrator team. A resource owned by a `group:<path>` principal MUST be migrated to a team whose sole member is that group at the `owner` role, created for the purpose when none exists; the team's slug is the group path's last segment lowercased with every character outside `[a-z0-9-]` replaced by `-`, suffixed with `-2`, `-3`, and so on when taken; the mapping MUST be audited. Existing administrator and operator login and group lists MUST be migrated into a platform administrator team and a platform operator team with policy rules granting the actions those roles gate today, as the route bindings of [RFC-0003:C-ENFORCEMENT](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-enforcement) record them; the existing cluster policy MUST be migrated into `dispatch` rules under [RFC-0003:C-CONDITIONS](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-conditions). A fresh install, or one whose platform administrator team has no membership that resolves to a user, MUST seed that team from configuration at startup and MUST NOT offer any request path that creates the first administrator. During migration a resource governed by both an existing guard and the new decision MUST be allowed only when both allow. The existing principal spellings `user:<login>` and `group:<path>` MUST remain valid and unchanged; `team:<slug>` and `run:<id>` are additive. The decisions that today define secret ownership and brought-cluster ownership will be amended to defer to this RFC on who may act; their custody, delivery, and probing content is untouched.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0003:C-TEAM-UX] Team-centric views (Normative) <a id="rfc-0003c-team-ux"></a>

The user interface MUST present governed resources filtered by an owner context the caller chooses among the principals they act as, with each team and the caller's own user principal as a context, and MUST include resources shared with that context. The owner picker on every creation surface MUST offer only the principals the caller acts as. A refusal MUST be shown with the reason the decision returned, verbatim. The interface MUST show the signed-in user's team memberships and roles as the controller resolves them, including memberships held through a group, a rule, or a nested team, and MUST show a resource's shares to anyone who may read it.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0003:C-RUN-PRINCIPAL] Run principal (Normative) <a id="rfc-0003c-run-principal"></a>

Every run MUST act under its own principal `run:<run id>`, proven by a credential issued at dispatch that proves only that run, and MUST NOT act under its launcher's or owner's credential. The run principal's subject set is the run principal alone; its actor is the owner principal of the launch that produced it. The default policy set MUST grant a run principal exactly: `read` on its launch, on itself, and on their children under [RFC-0003:C-HIERARCHY](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-hierarchy); and `publish` on itself, where `publish` is recording an output the launch's declared exposure permits under [RFC-0001:C-EXPOSURE](../rfc/RFC-0001.md#rfc-0001c-exposure). Task logs, artifacts, events, and spend are recorded through the pod-bound ingest surface that [RFC-0003:C-ENFORCEMENT](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-enforcement) places outside this contract and are not actions of the run principal. The grants of the policy set and vocabulary to authenticated user principals do not extend to run principals. A run credential MUST expire when the run reaches a terminal state and MUST be refused after that regardless of expiry. A request under a run principal for any resource outside its launch MUST return the not-found response of [RFC-0003:C-READ-SCOPING](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-read-scoping).

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0003:C-SHARING] Per-resource shares (Normative) <a id="rfc-0003c-sharing"></a>

A subject holding `share` on a governed resource MAY grant another principal a share role on that one resource. A share names the resource, the grantee principal, a share role from a fixed vocabulary of at least `viewer` (`read`), `launcher` (`read` and `launch`), and `editor` (`read`, `update`, `launch`, `bind`), and optionally a not-after time under [RFC-0003:C-CONDITIONS](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-conditions). A share role confers only the actions the resource type defines. A share MUST NOT confer `transfer`, `delete`, `share`, `approve`, `activate`, or `manage-members`, and a grant of a role containing any action the sharer does not hold on the resource MUST be refused rather than clipped. A share is a resource-scoped rule stored with the resource, outside the digested policy set of [RFC-0003:C-POLICY](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-policy); the shares on a resource are part of its `read`. A share MUST be revocable by any subject holding `share` on the resource or by a platform administrator, and MUST be audited on grant, change, and revocation. Transferring a resource MUST preserve its shares. A share on a parent applies to its children under [RFC-0003:C-HIERARCHY](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-hierarchy); a share is otherwise never inherited.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0003:C-HIERARCHY] Resource hierarchy (Normative) <a id="rfc-0003c-hierarchy"></a>

A governed resource MAY have exactly one parent resource, itself governed. A child MUST have the same owner as its parent, MUST inherit its parent's read scope and shares, and MUST NOT be transferred separately from its root. The parent relation is: a draft version's parent is its draft; a trigger's parent is its standing launch; a run's parent is the launch or standing launch that produced it; a run's task logs, artifacts, events, and spend records are children of the run; a binding's parent is its secret. Every spend record MUST carry, in addition to its inherited owner, the owner principal of its launch at the time of the spend; transfer changes the inherited owner and MUST NOT rewrite that attribution, so that spend sums by who spent it. Actions on a child that the vocabulary does not define for its type MUST resolve to the corresponding action on the nearest ancestor that defines it.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0003:C-CONDITIONS] Rule conditions (Normative) <a id="rfc-0003c-conditions"></a>

A policy rule or share MAY carry a not-after time; the decision MUST evaluate it against the controller's clock at decision time, and an expired rule or share MUST NOT allow anything. Expiry MUST be visible wherever the rule or share is listed. The `dispatch` action on a dispatch target MUST be decided per target through policy rules, so that which principals may dispatch onto which cluster or brought target is a policy fact and not a separate configuration; absent a rule, a target admits only its owner as [RFC-0003:C-POLICY](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-policy) grants, and a platform-owned target admits every authenticated user principal by the default policy set. A launch or firing whose subject may not `dispatch` onto its resolved target MUST be refused before any pod exists. The policy schema MUST admit both conditions from its first version; other conditions are later amendments.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0003:C-NAMES] Names are scoped to the owner (Normative) <a id="rfc-0003c-names"></a>

The human-readable identifier of a governed root resource (a playbook id, a draft id, a secret name, a provider id, a target name) MUST be unique within its owner, and two resources with different owners MAY share an identifier. Team slugs are unique per controller as [RFC-0003:C-PRINCIPALS](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-principals) requires. The API MUST address a governed resource by owner principal and identifier, with the owner principal carried as one percent-encoded path segment in its `<scheme>:<id>` spelling. The API MUST accept an unqualified identifier only where it resolves to exactly one resource the caller may read, and MUST refuse an ambiguous one as a conflict naming the count of candidates. Every existing resource keeps its identifier through the migration of [RFC-0003:C-COMPATIBILITY](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-compatibility), since assigning owners cannot create a collision within one owner.

*Since: v0.1.0*
